sources.behavior: The PTY connect handler closes 4404 when the session is not found or has exited and 1000 on a normal end, consumes the single-use ticket, accepts a cursor at or above -1, and sends the replay as PtyProtocol.chunks followed by the meta frame.
runPtySocket races the PTY output drain against the WebSocket input loop with Effect.raceFirst, so whichever side ends first ends both PTY doors' connections, and runs detach on every exit path.

A non-empty ticket query on a PTY connect, and a pairing link under /auth/connect/, skip the credential check, so the hand-written door authenticates the WebSocket upgrade with the ticket alone and a pairing code is redeemed with no other credential.

A request with no Origin header is allowed before any other origin rule (then a same-host origin, the localhost, 127.0.0.1, oc://renderer, Tauri, and opencode.ai origins, and the configured cors list); the SDK sends no Origin on its PTY WebSocket upgrades and relies on that first rule.
The ticket-issuing request carries the x-opencode-ticket header and the connect URL carries the ticket query.
The control frame is one 0x00 byte followed by UTF-8 JSON carrying the absolute cursor after replay, and replay arrives in REPLAY_CHUNK-sized frames.
PTY connect tickets are single-use and live 60 seconds.
The retained replay buffer is capped, exited sessions stay observable until they are removed, and attach replays from the requested cursor.
The PTY ticket service and the persistent-PTY service are wired into the server layer graph.
The handoff response is a single-key body whose handoff value is nullable, and the persistent connect endpoint reuses the PTY ticket query and header.
The persistent connect handler closes 4404 when the terminal is unavailable and 1000 on a normal end, consumes the ticket, and requires a cursor at or above 0.
The handoff call yields null when no daemon is running, and the service reports NotFoundError and UnavailableError.
The opencode-pty daemon wire protocol is version 7; the client refuses a daemon that registers another version.
The handoff record is the component PersistentPty.Handoff carrying the running daemon directory.
OPENCODE_PTY_BIN overrides the daemon executable; otherwise the embedded asset is installed under an opencode-pty directory keyed by version and checksum.
Under Node the daemon executable is OPENCODE_PTY_BIN or opencode-pty resolved on PATH.
The embedded daemon asset comes from the binaryPath export of the pty package.
The CLI package bin map names "opencode" as the installed command and keeps "opencode2" as a transitional alias of the same launcher, so the shipped launcher default resolves "opencode" from PATH.
The opencode-pty daemon dependency is pinned at 0.1.13, which fixes the daemon protocol the persistent-PTY door speaks.

A ticketed PTY connect is admitted before the server reports ready. Uncredentialed or wrongly credentialed requests above the API layer receive a 401 whose JSON body is the UnauthorizedError the document declares, with the Basic challenge only for requests that are not browser fetches. While the server is not ready, GET /api/info is answered by the process layer under Basic auth with the version, pid, urls, and paths.tmp body at 500 when failed or 503 when starting or stopping, the latter two with retry-after: 1; once ready the request reaches the API group's server.info handler, which answers the same shape at 200.
Behavioral oracle: the upstream suite asserts the 4404 close code, the null handoff body, and terminal survival across an explicit restart handoff.
Behavioral oracle: the reference client sends the ticket and cursor query parameters when it opens a PTY socket.

The ripgrep version upstream downloads on demand. CI provisions that exact version with pinned digests so an offline simulated server never has to reach the network for it, so a moved constant must be reviewed with the refresh rather than discovered as a failing filesystem live test.
Behavioral oracle: the TUI resumes a terminal from the snapshot tail cursor.

The standalone service decodes one JSON readiness object from the child's stdout, requiring only a string url member, and ends the server by closing its stdin, which is the contract the SDK's launcher is a parity port of. The endpoint it returns carries the child's pid and an exited effect (proc.exitCode) that yields the exit code, or fails with the terminating signal when a signal ended the child.

The spawner the standalone service starts its child through merges the command env over the parent environment when extendEnv is set, starts the child in its own process group off Windows, and ends it by killing the tree (taskkill /pid <pid> /T /F on Windows, process.kill(-pid, signal) elsewhere, falling back to the child alone) with killSignal, SIGTERM by default, escalating to SIGKILL once forceKillAfter elapses; after the child exits, its stdout and stderr share one 1-second deadline to close before they are discarded.

The npm launcher resolves the platform binary (OPENCODE_BIN_PATH, a cached copy, or the node_modules package walk), spawns it with stdio inherit, forwards SIGINT, SIGTERM, and SIGHUP (plus SIGUSR1 off Windows) to it, and mirrors its exit: it re-raises the child's terminating signal on itself or exits with the child's code (0 when there is none). An npm-installed opencode command is therefore a node process whose child is the real server.

In stdio mode the serve command prints exactly one JSON line carrying the bound url to stdout after full boot and exits when stdin reaches EOF, which is the readiness line ServerReadyLine parses and the lease OpenCodeServer releases. In service mode it changes into the user home (which ServerIsolation's isolated home relies on), returns at once when a compatible incumbent already answers, and exits 0 as the loser when another daemon holds the port and is recognized, which is the exit the Ensure election reads as a lost race and answers by doubling its spawn delay; a loser that exited non-zero would fail every multi-contender Ensure. On Windows, a service run from a package-manager or curl install first holds a second hard link to its own image under the cache directory, so an installer can replace the binary while the daemon runs; the pid and start time the stop door identifies it by are unchanged, and a daemon the stop door ends hard leaves that link for the next service start to sweep.

HTTP Basic credentials are checked against the fixed username opencode and the configured password, or a session token a pairing link issued, which the server accepts anywhere the password is, and authentication is required whenever a non-empty password is configured, which fixes the SDK's default Username and the rule that a CLI-started server always needs a password.

The request directory is resolved from location[directory] first, then the percent-decoded x-opencode-directory header, then the server working directory. The server no longer reads the workspace query or header, which defines the hand-written directory-only LocationSelector contract.

Session-scoped routes take their location from the session row that the sessionID route parameter names, so the request's location[directory] query and x-opencode-directory header do not select the location there; an invalid session ID is InvalidRequestError and a missing session is SessionNotFoundError.

Session form routes take their location from the session row like other session routes, except that the sessionID "global" skips the session lookup and takes the location from the request (location[directory] query, then the x-opencode-directory header, then the server working directory).
The global event stream sends server.connected as its first frame and a heartbeat every 15 seconds, which the SSE door's first-frame handling and idle expectations depend on.
Each event subscriber is buffered at 4,096 events and frames are written as data: lines only, which the SDK's SSE parser and its backpressure assumptions depend on.

The first-party client's event connection aborts an attempt that has not delivered server.connected within 2 seconds, aborts a connected stream that stays silent for the idle timeout (45 seconds by default), waits 1 second before reconnecting unless a resync forced the reconnect or the first failed attempt's reconnect hook resolved a new server, and resubscribes without a Last-Event-ID, so it never asks the server to replay missed events.

Event persistence is off unless the host enables it, a durable replay yields events strictly after the requested sequence, and log.synced marks the replay boundary, which the session-log replay contract and the CLI-profile live test depend on.

The session list declares limit, order and cursor, where order applies to the first page only and the opaque cursor carries the continuation, which the cursor-list spine and CursorSequence depend on; the file is also the Restore patch preimage for the SSE payloads.

sources.behavior: The tagged error catalogue declares the wire discriminators the typed error family maps, so an added, removed or renamed tag changes the SDK's error union.
The published package's bin map names opencode as the command and opencode2 as the legacy alias of the same binary, which is the contract behind the launcher's default command.
The message list declares limit, order, cursor and a type filter that must be passed again on every continuation, which the message-list spine, CursorSequence and EnumerateMessagesAsync depend on.

sources.behavior: Info is the registration record a service publishes: an optional id and version, the raw url string, a positive integer pid, and an optional password; the SDK's strict registration reader admits exactly these members.

The Promise-client ensure loop, the statement-level template ServiceElection follows (ADR-0025; the Effect Service.ensure is the behaviour source and states the same election): a wall-clock deadline loop that reuses a ready compatible service, reports a failed one without spawning, replaces a version-mismatched one, and after three consecutive info-probe timeouts on the same registration announces missing, clears the handoff sidecar, terminates the unresponsive daemon, and spawns a replacement while keeping one contender plus one lock probe alive.

The persistent-terminal handoff sidecar lives beside the registration file under the .pty-handoff suffix, written exclusively at mode 0600 through a temporary file and a rename; clear removes it and treats a missing file as already cleared, which is what a stop without a handoff does before it signals.

discover reads the registration file and probes /api/info with its Basic credential under the request timeout. The probe compares pid and the recorded version; an authenticated 404 (an older daemon still serving /api/status) marks the registered service incompatible without decoding a body. Discovery returns only a ready, compatible service whose version matches when requested. ensure repeats that probe every pollInterval until a compatible ready service answers, keeping one contender plus one lock probe alive while the registration is unresolved and replacing an incompatible service, and gives up after promiseTimeout of wall-clock time rather than after a fixed attempt count. stop reads the registration, prepares a persistent-terminal handoff only when asked for one and clears the sidecar otherwise, then terminate re-reads the registration and compares id, version, url, and pid before every signal: SIGTERM, a poll of stopPollAttempts spaced stopPollInterval, SIGKILL when the process is still there, the same poll again, and the registration removed only when it is still the same record; a process still running after SIGKILL fails the stop and leaves the record in place.

The client's timing constants: a 2-second info request timeout, the 25 ms poll spacing, the spawn delays, and the stop poll ServiceTiming.Default mirrors value for value, plus the 120-second promiseTimeout that bounds the ensure loop by wall clock, which Ensure reads at its own pin.
A discovered service matches only when its reported version equals the expected one ordinally, and any version matches when none is expected; ExpectedVersion applies the same rule.

The release channels latest, dev, beta, and next share service.json; every other channel is sanitized into service-<channel>.json; a legacy SHA-1 filename exists for every channel except latest and local; versionBelongsToChannel admits the exact installed version or the 0.0.0-<channel>-N[.M] spelling; migration copies a donor exclusively with mode 0600 and ignores write failures. Info declares an optional boolean disabled key beside hostname, port, password, cors, and env, and read turns any decode failure into an empty config, so an invalid document is absent config.

The service writes its registration atomically through a temp file and rename with mode 0600, carrying id, the compiled version, the bound url, its own pid, and the password, then re-reads the file every five seconds and shuts down when another instance replaced it.
A source run compiles the version and channel as the literal local, which is the channel and version the managed-service fixture registers under.
OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR replaces the whole config root with no opencode segment beneath it, and OPENCODE_TEST_HOME replaces the home directory service mode changes into.
Each global root is its XDG variable when set and non-empty, otherwise the home-relative default: .local/share, .cache, .config, and .local/state.
Hash.fast is a hex SHA-1 digest of the UTF-8 input, the function the legacy registration filename is derived from.
The service status states starting, ready, failed, and stopping are what the health handler maps to 503, 200, 500, and 503.

The info answer carries version, pid, urls, and paths.tmp; pid may be zero for a runtime without an OS process identity. The background-service probe revalidates the registered process identity and expected version.

Upstream's own discovery expectations: a compatible registered service is reused, a waiting one is awaited, a failed one is reported without spawning, and a legacy health answer is replaced; ServiceEnsurerTests, ServiceDiscoveryTests, and the Ensure live tests re-prove them.

Upstream's own filename and channel expectations: the release channels share service.json, custom channels are sanitized, and version-to-channel membership follows the pre-release spelling; ServicePathResolverTests and ServiceMigrationTests re-prove them.

The version gate is opt-in: service options only require a matching version when the caller asks for the check, which is why ExpectedVersion is null by default; ServiceSelectionTests and ServiceVersionPolicyTests re-prove it.

sources.behavior: Upstream's end-to-end service smoke asserts that the daemon it built writes a registration carrying the service identity (id, version, pid); it is a check on the daemon's output, not a client rule, and the SDK's reader still admits a registration without an id, as the client's own Info schema does.

resolve routes the default CLI connection to Standalone.start when args.standalone is set or the service config's disabled is true, before any managed-service path; otherwise it goes through ServiceConfig.options, which performs legacy registration migration before discovery or ensure and enables the version gate only when mismatch is not ignore. An explicit --server connection uses server.info with a five-second bound and warns on a version mismatch. shutdownPersistentPty discovers with no version filter and, when a service answers, calls persistentPty.shutdown with no request bound; the managed restart stops with a handoff and ensures again.
The CLI reads the server password from OPENCODE_PASSWORD and falls back to the legacy OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD; the session environment it hands on omits both.

The CLI stop command resolves the channel options, asks the registered service to shut its persistent terminals down and ignores every failure of that request, then runs Service.stop, which clears the sidecar and terminates the registered process.

The workspace catalog pins the Effect release the protocol document is generated with, whose JSON Schema encoding of StructWithRest (a struct's properties beside a single-element allOf carrying only the rest's additionalProperties) the projector admits as an open object, and whose union decode (SchemaAST Union.getParser: literal sentinels, then the first member in declaration order that decodes) the structural union first-match arm mirrors, as tools/oracles/first-match-union.ts proves; an Effect bump is reviewed against both, and the oracle re-run, before the snapshot moves.

A contender is spawned detached with stdin and stdout ignored, stderr piped, and the parent environment overlaid; stderr is retained as an 8 KiB tail, error and close are observed, the child is unref'd, and release drops the listener without signalling, which is the contract the Ensure door's spawn seam ports.

DEFAULT_REDACT_JSON_FIELDS lists the JSON fields upstream's HTTP recorder masks in every recorded body (access_token, api_key, apikey, client_secret, password, refresh_token, secret, token), matched after normalizeField drops every character outside [a-z0-9] and lower-cases; the list and the rule are the generator's redaction floor for generated ToString (ADR-0028, SecretMemberPolicy), so a change to either moves the floor.

ENV_SECRET_NAMES is the case-insensitive marker-word pattern upstream reads as a secret in an environment-variable name (API, AUTH, BEARER, CREDENTIAL, KEY, PASSWORD, SECRET, TOKEN, anywhere in the name); the generator's secret-name wall stops a model member whose wire name matches it until a curation row decides it (ADR-0028, SecretMemberPolicy).

The CLI's entry runs every command through NodeRuntime.runMain with its error reporting off, writes a fatal cause to stderr itself, and exits with process.exitCode (0 when unset): the stderr tail and exit status a contender's failure report carries, and the exit 0 the Ensure election reads as a loser that stood down.
serve --service runs the server process in service mode, the flag behind Ensure's default command (opencode serve --service); --service and --stdio cannot be combined.

Upstream's service fixture modes (failed, delayed, coordinated losers, a stalled or stale registered service) are what the SDK fixture's contender-probe stand-ins imitate, so the Ensure live tests exercise the same situations the upstream client tests do.

Upstream codegen turns a route whose path ends in a single trailing wildcard into a required string input named path, or wildcard when an input already takes path, and fills it with encodePath: each slash-separated segment through encodeURIComponent; the generator route-tail rule mirrors both (ADR-0029), and tools/oracles/wildcard-path.ts re-proves the encoding against the generated client.

The fs.read handler takes the wildcard tail from the request URL path, percent-decodes it, reads the file relative to the location and answers its raw bytes under the file MIME type, which the route tail and the binary envelope (Content, ContentType) rely on.
